title: CLCON/46/2016 of Neeru Pandey Neeru Vs R.k. Kunwar AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
CLCON No. 46 of 2016
U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. Yogesh Bhatt, Advocate for the
petitioner/applicant.
By means of present contempt petition, the
petitioner/applicant seeks to summon the contemnors
personally before this Court and initiate contempt
proceedings against opposite parties and punish them
for willfully and deliberately committing contempt of
this Court by flouting the order dated 4.9.2015 passed
in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 125 of 2015.
On 4.9.2015 this Court passed the following
order in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 125 of 2015 which is
as follows:
"Respondent no. 2 Director Education
(Secondary) is hereby directed to hear the
petitioner, in person, and he shall take the
decision on her representation for transfer in
the light of gravity of ailment vis-à-vis
concerning Rules in this regard, as quickly as
possible, but not later than three weeks from
the date of receiving the certified copy of this
order."
It is the statement of learned counsel for the
petitioner/applicant although the petitioner was heard
by respondent, but her representation has not been
decided, as yet.
Instead of issuing contempt notice, this Court
deems it appropriate to reiterate order dated 4.9.2015
by directing opposite party no. 1 to decide the pending
representation of the petitioner/applicant for transfer,
in accordance with order dated 4.9.2015, at the earliest
possible.
Petitioner/applicant is directed to get a copy of
this order served upon opposite party no. 1 who is
directed to do the needful in the light of order dated
4.9.2015 failing which it will be presumed that the
opposite has nothing to say in the matter and shall be
liable for appropriate action in the Contempt of Courts
Act.
